# rasuvaeff/property-testing-core

Framework-agnostic property-based testing engine for PHP 8.3+: generators with
integrated shrinking, a structured property runner, a regression corpus,
lifecycle events, and stateful/model-based testing. No test-framework
dependency. Adapters: `rasuvaeff/property-testing-testo` (Testo `#[Property]`),
`rasuvaeff/property-testing-phpunit` (PHPUnit trait). Domain generators:
`rasuvaeff/property-testing-names` (`Names::first()`/`last()`/`middle()`/
`full()`/`person()` over bundled `en`/`ru` person-name datasets). Conflicts
with the frozen `rasuvaeff/property-testing` 2.x (same namespace).

## Install

```
composer require --dev rasuvaeff/property-testing-core
```

Runtime deps: PHP `8.3 - 8.5`, `ext-mbstring`, `ext-random`.

## Rules

- The runner NEVER reads environment variables, never prints, never exits, and
  never throws to report a property outcome — it returns a structured
  `PropertyResult`. `PROPERTY_RUNS`/`PROPERTY_SEED`/`PROPERTY_VERBOSE`/
  `PROPERTY_DB` are adapter conventions; the only env helper here is
  `FilesystemCorpus::fromEnv()` (reads `PROPERTY_DB` when YOU call it).
- Sequential-only: `Classify` and the in-body draw tape are process-local
  statics armed/drained around each body execution. Do not run properties
  concurrently in one process.
- A listener exception ABORTS the run (infrastructure failure, deliberately not
  caught); a listener can never change a property's outcome.
- Configuration errors (`runs < 1`, missing generator, mismatched parameter
  names) throw; property verdicts come back as results.
- `Random` uses an object-scoped MT19937 engine (`\Random\Randomizer`) — same
  seed, same sequence, regardless of other random calls. NOT cryptographic.
- A generator NEVER yields an out-of-domain value: `Gen::filter()` and sized
  collections throw `GenerationExhausted` when they cannot satisfy their
  predicate/minimum. Construct dependent values with `Gen::flatMap()` /
  `Gen::draw()` instead of filtering broadly.
- `runs` means successful checks; `Assume::that(false)` discards the attempt.
  Discards are capped by `maxDiscards` (default `runs * 10`) -> `GaveUp`.
- Shrinking is integrated: `generate(Random)` returns a `Shrinkable` (value +
  lazy tree of smaller candidates). There is NO `shrink(mixed)` method. Greedy
  per-parameter descent; best-effort minimal.
- Corpus format is byte-compatible with `rasuvaeff/property-testing` 2.8
  (`FORMAT_VERSION` 1): one JSON file per property, max 8 values + 2 seed
  entries. Seed entries are fenced off by `FilesystemCorpus::SEQUENCE_EPOCH`.
- A corpus values entry stores the failing input VERBATIM as plain JSON, so the
  corpus directory is as sensitive as what the generators produce. Do not put
  it in world-readable paths or published build artifacts; for realistic
  personal/credential-shaped data, synthesise inside the property body instead
  of generating it, so only a seed is recorded.
- Results serialize natively when traces carry no argument values
  (`zend.exception_ignore_args=1`); the portable format is
  `CounterExample::toArray()` / `toJson()`.

## Core API

### Running a property

```php
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Gen;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Runner\CallableTrialExecutor;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Runner\Falsified;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Runner\PropertyConfig;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Runner\PropertyDefinition;
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Runner\PropertyRunner;

$definition = new PropertyDefinition(
    id: 'suite::name',              // keys events and the corpus
    name: 'name',                   // display name in failure messages
    generators: ['x' => Gen::int()],// one ArbitraryInterface per parameter
    parameterNames: ['x'],          // declaration order
    config: new PropertyConfig(
        runs: 100,          // successful checks (>= 1)
        seed: null,         // null -> random, reported on failure
        maxShrinks: null,   // cap on ACCEPTED shrink steps; 0 = no shrinking
        maxDiscards: null,  // null -> runs * 10
        timeoutMs: null,    // per-run wall-clock deadline
        budgetMs: null,     // whole-random-phase wall-clock budget
    ),
    examples: [],               // list of positional tuples, run FIRST, unshrunk
    replayRegressions: true,    // adapters pass false when the seed is pinned
);

$result = (new PropertyRunner())->run(
    $definition,
    new CallableTrialExecutor(static function (int $x): void {
        // return = pass; Assume::that() = discard; any throwable = failure
    }),
    listeners: [],   // iterable<PropertyListener>
    corpus: null,    // ?Corpus — null means no replay, no filesystem access
);
```

`PropertyRunner::__construct(?Clock $clock = null)` — inject a `Clock` fake for
deterministic deadline/budget tests; `MonotonicClock` is the default.

### Results (closed hierarchy, `Runner\` namespace)

Every result implements `PropertyResult` (`failure(): ?Throwable`, null = pass):

- `Passed` — carries `RunStatistics` ($attempts, $discards, $checks,
  $classifications per label).
- `Falsified` — carries `PropertyViolationException`;
  `counterExample(): CounterExample` (`seed`, `runsBeforeFailure`,
  `originalArguments`, `shrunkArguments`, `shrinkSteps`, `shrinkTrials`,
  `skips`, `failure`, `toArray()`, `toJson()`, `toExamplesCode()`).
- `GaveUp` — `GaveUpException` + `RunStatistics` (discard budget exhausted).
- `CoverageFailed` — `CoverageViolationException` + `RunStatistics`
  (a `Classify::cover()` requirement missed although every run passed).
- `DeadlineExceeded` — `DeadlineExceededException` (one run overran timeoutMs).
- `TimeBudgetExceeded` — `TimeBudgetExceededException` + `RunStatistics`.
- `GenerationFailed` — `GenerationExhausted`.
- `ExampleFailed` — `ExampleViolationException` (explicit example failed).
- `RegressionFailed` — `RegressionViolationException` (`getArguments()`,
  `getSeed()`) — a corpus values entry still fails.

Executor seam: implement `TrialExecutor` (`execute(array $arguments):
TrialOutcome`) to adapt any framework; `TrialOutcome::passed() / failed($e) /
discarded()`. `CallableTrialExecutor` is the standalone implementation.

### Corpus (`Runner\` namespace)

```php
interface Corpus {
    /** @return list<CorpusEntry> */
    public function recall(string $id, array $parameterNames): array;
    public function remember(string $id, CounterExample $ce, array $parameterNames): void;
    public function prune(string $id, CorpusEntry $entry): void;
}

new FilesystemCorpus('/path/to/dir');   // 2.8-compatible JSON storage
FilesystemCorpus::fromEnv();            // ?self from PROPERTY_DB
```

Values entries (data-representable minimised input) replay as ONE run; seed
entries (objects/closures/draws in the counterexample) re-run the whole random
phase and are dropped when `SEQUENCE_EPOCH` changes.

### Events (`Event\` namespace, all implement `PropertyEvent`)

`PropertyStarted(propertyId, seed, runs)`, `ExampleStarted/ExampleFinished`,
`RunStarted(attempt, arguments)`, `RunPassed(labels, elapsedNs)`,
`RunDiscarded`, `RunFailed(failure, elapsedNs)`, `ShrinkTried(parameter,
candidate, accepted)`, `ShrinkAccepted(step, parameter, before, after)`,
`CorpusReplayed/CorpusPruned/CorpusStored`, `PropertyFinished(?failure)`.

```php
interface PropertyListener { public function onEvent(PropertyEvent $event): void; }
```

### Static facade: `Gen`

```php
use Rasuvaeff\PropertyTesting\Gen;

Gen::int()                              // IntArbitrary, PHP_INT_MIN..PHP_INT_MAX, shrinks to 0
Gen::intBetween(int $min, int $max)     // IntArbitrary, [$min, $max]
Gen::intPositive()                      // IntArbitrary, 1..PHP_INT_MAX
Gen::float()                            // FloatArbitrary, [0.0, 1.0)
Gen::floatBetween(float $min, float $max)  // FloatArbitrary, [$min, $max]
Gen::bool()                             // BoolArbitrary
Gen::string()                           // StringArbitrary, Unicode, len 0..100
Gen::stringAscii()                      // StringArbitrary, printable ASCII
Gen::stringOf(int $minLen, int $maxLen) // StringArbitrary, bounded length
Gen::stringFrom(string $alphabet, int $minLen = 0, int $maxLen = 100) // CharsetStringArbitrary
Gen::bytes(int $minLen = 0, int $maxLen = 100)  // BytesArbitrary, raw bytes
Gen::arrayOf(ArbitraryInterface $el, int $min = 0, int $max = 100)  // ArrayArbitrary
Gen::nonEmptyArrayOf(ArbitraryInterface $el, int $max = 100)        // ArrayArbitrary, >= 1
Gen::uniqueArrayOf(ArbitraryInterface $el, int $min = 0, int $max = 100) // UniqueArrayArbitrary
Gen::subset(array $values, int $minSize = 0, ?int $maxSize = null)  // SubsetArbitrary: subsets of a fixed ordered set; source duplicates rejected (InvalidArgumentException); size uniform over [min, max] (null max = full size); keeps source order; shrinks size first, then elements toward earlier source positions; no discards
Gen::dictOf(ArbitraryInterface $key, ArbitraryInterface $value, int $min = 0, int $max = 100) // DictionaryArbitrary
Gen::record(array $shape)               // RecordArbitrary, fixed-shape map
Gen::oneOf(mixed ...$values)            // OneOfArbitrary
Gen::elements(array $values)            // OneOfArbitrary (array form)
Gen::enum(SomeEnum::class)              // OneOfArbitrary over enum cases
Gen::constant(mixed $value)             // ConstantArbitrary
Gen::char()                             // StringArbitrary, one ASCII char
Gen::uuid()                             // UuidArbitrary, v4 UUIDs
Gen::datetime(?DateTimeImmutable $min, ?DateTimeImmutable $max) // DateTimeArbitrary, UTC
Gen::floatSpecial()                     // OneOfArbitrary over NAN/±INF/-0.0/float edges
Gen::intRange(int $min, int $max)       // FlatMappedArbitrary: ordered [lo, hi]
Gen::recursive(ArbitraryInterface $leaf, Closure $wrap, int $maxDepth = 3)
Gen::nullable(ArbitraryInterface $inner)        // NullableArbitrary
Gen::map(ArbitraryInterface $inner, Closure $fn)     // MappedArbitrary
Gen::flatMap(ArbitraryInterface $inner, Closure $fn) // FlatMappedArbitrary, dependent domains
Gen::filter(ArbitraryInterface $inner, Closure $p)   // FilteredArbitrary, 100 retries then GenerationExhausted
Gen::tuple(ArbitraryInterface ...$elements)          // TupleArbitrary
Gen::frequency(iterable $pairs)                      // FrequencyArbitrary, [weight, arb] pairs
Gen::commands(mixed $initialModel, array $commandGenerators, int $minLen = 0, int $maxLen = 100) // CommandSequenceArbitrary
Gen::ipv4()  Gen::ipv6()  Gen::email()  Gen::url()  // ipv6: canonical RFC 5952 text, shrinks to "::"
Gen::json(int $maxDepth = 3)  Gen::jsonString(int $maxDepth = 3)
Gen::regex(string $pattern, int $maxRepeat = 8)          // regex SUBSET compiled to combinators
Gen::stringMatching(string $pattern, int $maxRepeat = 8) // alias of regex()
Gen::draw(ArbitraryInterface $arb)      // in-body dependent draw; ONLY inside a running property body
Gen::sample(ArbitraryInterface $arb, int $count = 10, int $seed = 0)        // eager debug helper
Gen::sampleShrinks(ArbitraryInterface $arb, int $seed = 0, int $limit = 10) // value + first shrink candidates
```

Numeric generators are boundary-biased (~1 in 5 draws returns an in-range edge
value). Sized generators never go below their minimum.

### Shrink trees: `Shrinkable`

```php
Shrinkable::leaf(mixed $value): Shrinkable   // terminal node
Shrinkable::of(mixed $value, Closure(): iterable<Shrinkable> $shrinks): Shrinkable
$s->value; $s->shrinks(); $s->map($fn);
```

Custom generators implement `ArbitraryInterface::generate(Random): Shrinkable`.
Draw randomness only via the injected `Random` (`int()`, `float()`, `bytes()`).
Keep every branch finite; never yield a candidate equal to its parent.

### Body helpers

```php
Assume::that(bool $condition): void   // throws AssumptionSkipped -> discard
Classify::label(string $label): void
Classify::when(bool $condition, string $label): void
Classify::cover(bool $condition, string $label, float $minPercent): void // -> CoverageFailed
Gen::draw(ArbitraryInterface $arb): mixed  // recorded on the replay tape, shrunk like a parameter
```

`ValueRenderer::render(mixed $value): string` — the single-line human rendering
used inside counterexample messages; adapters reuse it for verbose output.

### Stateful / model-based (`StateMachine\` namespace)

```php
interface Command extends \Stringable {
    public function preCondition(mixed $model): bool;
    public function nextState(mixed $model): mixed;          // pure, returns NEW model
    public function run(mixed $model, mixed $system): mixed; // execute against the SUT
    public function postCondition(mixed $model, mixed $result): bool; // false/throw = falsify
}

// In the body:
StateMachine::check(CommandSequence $sequence, Closure $systemFactory): void;
// throws PostconditionViolation naming the failing step
```

`Gen::commands()` builds valid-by-construction sequences; shrinking drops
command blocks then simplifies each command's parameters; replay skips commands
whose precondition a dropped step invalidated.
